title: Frame — Movie-Suggestion
description: A content-based ML movie discovery website with mood search, explainable TF-IDF recommendations, personal ratings and a watchlist.
notes: Working local website with a curated 24-film catalog. Uses classical content-based ML, not LLM inference or fake confidence percentages.
20 unit/HTTP tests and desktop/mobile workflows passed. Source published on the completed-web-app branch; no hosted backend demo.
One local profile; no public authentication, streaming-availability feed or live deployment is implied.

title: Waypoint — Currency Exchange
description: A clear currency and travel-budget planner with Decimal arithmetic, fee-aware conversion, dated rates, history and explicit stale-data warnings.
notes: Fictional demo rates work offline and are visibly labeled. Optional Frankfurter reference-rate mode never silently falls back to fake data.
20 unit/HTTP tests and desktop/mobile workflows passed. Provider calls are mocked; no financial transfers or advice.
20 unit/HTTP tests and desktop/mobile workflows passed. Source published on the completed-web-app branch; no hosted backend demo.

title: Evidence RAG Studio
description: A citation-first document question-answering pipeline with an optional live model adapter.
notes: Deterministic overlapping text chunking and BM25 retrieval with document/chunk citations.
Abstains when there is no lexical evidence; local mode returns excerpts, not simulated LLM inference.
Optional OpenAI chat-completions adapter; sends only selected context and treats retrieved documents as untrusted.
Bounded document size, retrieved-context budget and explicit provider errors.
Published in its own public GitHub repository; source and tests are available. No hosted backend demo.

Offline mode is extractive retrieval, not a generative model. Live mode requires internet, OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_MODEL; API use may cost money. The adapter has unit tests with a mocked HTTP response, not a real provider test. Lexical retrieval is weaker than embeddings for paraphrases. Prompt instructions reduce risk but cannot guarantee injection resistance. Do not send sensitive documents to an external provider without approval.

title: LLM Eval Workbench
description: A reproducible regression gate for saved model responses.
notes: Versioned rubric checks for required phrases, forbidden content, citation format, refusal and JSON-schema-like requirements.
Per-case pass/fail evidence and aggregate checks, case scores and release threshold.
Compares baseline and candidate runs to expose regressions.
Exports structured results suitable for CI; no paid inference is needed.
Published in its own public GitHub repository; source and tests are available. No hosted backend demo.

This is a rule-based LLM evaluation harness, not an LLM and not a comprehensive safety evaluator. It evaluates supplied responses; it does not generate them. Phrase checks can be gamed and do not measure semantic truth. No external model was evaluated.

title: Churn Risk Lab
description: An interpretable binary-classification experiment with train-only scaling.
notes: Deterministic stratified train/test split on synthetic customer observations.
From-scratch logistic regression with L2 regularization and numerically stable sigmoid.
Held-out precision, recall, F1, accuracy, ROC AUC and a confusion matrix.
Standardized coefficient importance and an explicit majority-class baseline.
Published in its own public GitHub repository; source and tests are available. No hosted backend demo.

Synthetic educational dataset only; no real customer or business accuracy claims. The test set must not be used for repeated hyperparameter selection. This model is not suitable for decisions about real people without validation, consent, fairness analysis and monitoring. Features are numeric only. No deployment or persisted model registry is included.

title: Demand Forecast Lab
description: Leakage-conscious time-series forecasting with rolling-origin backtests.
notes: Regular daily date validation and deterministic seasonal synthetic demand.
Seven-day seasonal-naive and linear trend + weekday regression models.
Rolling-origin holdouts with MAE, RMSE and WAPE; chooses the lower-MAE model.
Refits the selected model on all historical observations to forecast the next 1–30 days.
Published in its own public GitHub repository; source and tests are available. No hosted backend demo.

Educational daily-demand model, not a promise of future business accuracy. Requires at least 42 consecutive daily nonnegative observations; irregular dates and missing values are rejected. Backtest selection can still overfit a short history. No holidays, exogenous regressors, probabilistic intervals or real retail data are included.

title: Roadmap Voting Board
description: A persistent feature-request board with idempotent voting and a responsive browser client.
notes: SQLite-backed idea creation and vote counts with unique voter/idea constraints.
Duplicate votes are idempotent; user-generated titles are rendered as text, never HTML.
Browser form, ranked ideas, refresh and visible API errors.
Local-only HTTP server, same-origin checks, JSON-only mutations and body limits.
Published in its own public GitHub repository; source and tests are available. No hosted backend demo.

A single-user/local reference app, not a production multi-user platform. Voter IDs are client-generated pseudonyms, not authenticated identities; users can create another ID and vote again. There is no organizer account, moderation, login, anti-fraud system or public hosting. The default demo command uses an in-memory database; server mode persists .data/app.sqlite3.

title: Conflict-Free Booking
description: A reservation API and planner that atomically rejects overlapping room bookings.
notes: BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions serialize conflicting booking attempts.
UTC-normalized timezone-aware intervals and half-open overlap rules.
Idempotency keys return the original reservation; mismatched reuse is rejected.
Responsive booking form, room/date display, persistent storage and conflict feedback.
Published in its own public GitHub repository; source and tests are available. No hosted backend demo.

Local educational scheduler without accounts, cancellations, notifications or authorization. Accepts any timezone-aware ISO timestamps; browser inputs are interpreted in the viewer’s local timezone then sent as UTC. Adjacent bookings are allowed. A single SQLite database is appropriate only for local/small workloads.

title: Durable Worker Queue
description: A container-oriented SQLite job queue with leases, retry and dead-letter handling.
notes: Atomic claim transactions, bounded attempts and lease-expiry recovery.
Idempotent enqueue keys prevent duplicate jobs; successful completion checks ownership.
Real worker process handles safe allowlisted sum and word-count jobs without eval or shell execution.
Non-root Docker image, persistent volume, healthcheck and API/worker Compose services.
Published in its own public GitHub repository; source and tests are available. No hosted backend demo.

At-least-once execution: jobs must be idempotent and side-effect-safe. SQLite is for one host and a shared local filesystem, not a distributed Redis/Kafka replacement. Lease renewal is not implemented; only short jobs are allowed. The Docker runtime was not available during construction, so image builds and Compose execution were not tested. Local process and queue state-machine tests are included.

title: Container Guard
description: A deterministic Dockerfile and Compose configuration review tool.
notes: Handles Dockerfile continuation lines and comments before evaluating policies.
Flags root user, unpinned bases, missing healthchecks and broad COPY patterns.
Reviews Compose privileged mode, host networking, Docker socket mounts and secret-looking environment names.
Returns evidence, severity and remediation hints without executing containers or shell commands.
Published in its own public GitHub repository; source and tests are available. No hosted backend demo.

Static heuristic review, not a vulnerability scanner or security certification. It cannot inspect image contents, CVEs, runtime privileges outside the supplied config, build-stage reachability or resolved environment values. Supply Compose as a parsed JSON object; the bundled compose.yaml is JSON-compatible YAML. Real environment values are never required.

title: Data Contract Pipeline
description: A CSV-to-SQLite ingestion pipeline with contracts, quarantine and lineage.
notes: Declarative column types, required values, uniqueness, ranges and allowed values.
Invalid records are quarantined with row-level reasons; valid rows are ingested transactionally.
Content-addressed batch IDs make repeated input ingestion idempotent.
Batch lineage records accepted/rejected counts; previews and SQL row counts are returned.
Published in its own public GitHub repository; source and tests are available. No hosted backend demo.

Single-file educational ETL, not an orchestrator or warehouse service. Contract column names are validated, values are parameterized and identifiers are quoted. All rows are held in memory, capped at 10000; CSV inputs are limited to 500 KB. Contract changes intentionally create separate batches. No external databases or personal datasets are bundled.

title: Cloud Capacity Planner
description: A queueing-theory capacity planner and seeded discrete-event simulation.
notes: Erlang-C wait probability, utilization and expected response for stable M/M/c queues.
Searches worker counts against a target probability of waiting beyond an SLO threshold.
Seeded heap-based simulation estimates queue wait, response percentiles and completed jobs.
Reports hourly cost from user-supplied rates, with unstable capacity rejected.
Published in its own public GitHub repository; source and tests are available. No hosted backend demo.

Assumes Poisson arrivals, independent exponential service times and identical workers. Costs are inputs, not live cloud prices. Simulated percentiles are estimates with finite-sample variation; no startup/transient correction or confidence intervals are included. This tool does not provision cloud resources or incur cloud charges.

title: EventOps Pro
description: A full-stack event operations suite connecting registration, QR attendance, feedback, resources, task scheduling and verified certificates.
notes: Seven connected modules: event registration and waitlists, QR/token check-in, feedback analytics, protected resources, dependency-aware tasks, participant dashboards and PDF certificates.
Organizer and participant permissions, session authentication, CSRF protection and audit logs are enforced by the backend.
16 backend integration tests passed; desktop and mobile workflows were checked. Docker setup and deployment documentation are included.
Runnable project source; the EventOps application itself is not deployed as a live demo.

title: Agentic Diagnostic Assistant for Kubernetes Operations
description: Completed TCS Xcelerate program project area, showcased with a new deterministic Kubernetes diagnostic reference implementation.
notes: TCS Xcelerate Program completed, as confirmed by Ahwan. This is a new reference implementation, not recovered original TCS training source.
Five deterministic specialists cover diagnosis, analysis, remediation planning, execution and safety supervision; no LLM or Google ADK inference is implemented.
Fixed read-only kubectl observations, SQLite audit storage, signed short-lived human approvals and dry-run execution by default.
The rebuild does not implement Google ADK, Slack approvals, log collection, arbitrary remediation, image updates or scaling. Approval does not enable unrestricted commands.
Source is currently in a private GitHub repository. Repository access is required; no hosted backend demo is available.

title: Mini-Redis
description: A Redis-compatible key-value server built over raw TCP, with RESP parsing and expiry.
notes: Streaming RESP parser without a third-party protocol library.
Commands include PING, SET, GET, DEL, INCR and TTL, with passive and background expiration.
The added web interface uses the repository’s Python twin in-process; it does not control the separate Java server.

title: MiniDB
description: An embedded relational engine with its own page format, buffer pool and B+ tree.
notes: 4 KB slotted pages, free-space bitmap, LRU buffer pool and dirty-page tracking.
Persistent on-disk B+ tree with leaf splits and range scans.
SQL subset supports CREATE, INSERT, SELECT, DELETE, WHERE and ORDER BY.

title: LaptopHub
description: A React e-commerce application with filtering, a cart, wishlist and responsive layouts.
notes: The CV reports a 95+ Lighthouse performance score and approximately 40% improved product discoverability.
Cart and wishlist use Context API; layouts support phone, tablet and desktop, with dark mode.
No verified repository or live deployment link was supplied for this project.

title: Memory-backed ReAct Agent
description: Working, episodic and semantic memory that can update facts instead of accumulating stale preferences.
notes: Hashed embeddings and cosine similarity support memory retrieval.
Calculator and memory tools are integrated into a ReAct loop.
The repository runs offline with a heuristic MockLLM; this portfolio does not imply live model inference.

title: minic · C Compiler
description: A subset C compiler that turns source code into x86-64 System V assembly.
notes: Recursive-descent parsing, type handling, local stack offsets and code generation.
Supports integer expressions, pointers, functions, conditionals and loops.
The browser interface compiles submitted source to assembly only; it does not execute submitted programs.

title: Private Meta-search
description: Self-hosted search infrastructure with aggregation, rate limiting and cleaner result URLs.
notes: SearXNG stack with Redis rate limiting, reverse-proxy TLS and client-IP stripping.
Python aggregator runs engines in parallel, removes tracking parameters and re-ranks results.
Offline catalog and optional live Wikipedia mode are distinct from the SearXNG deployment.

title: Snapshot & Rollback Engine
description: My Wipro embedded-training project: a Linux storage engine with copy-on-write blocks, named snapshots and CRC-32 integrity checks.
notes: Completed as the project for Wipro’s embedded training program.
Immutable append-only block records and atomic metadata replacement.
Named snapshots, rollback, persistence and integrity verification.
An optional character driver is separate from the user-space engine.

title: CPU Scheduler & Deadlock Simulator
description: Operating-system simulations for scheduling and safe resource allocation.
notes: FCFS and Round Robin scheduling implementations described in the CV.
Banker’s Algorithm rejects unsafe allocations.
No verified repository or live deployment link was supplied.

title: Expense Tracker
description: A persistent Python/SQLite expense ledger with validation and spending reports.
notes: Add, view and delete expenses; money is stored as integer cents.
Monthly and category reports use SQL aggregation.
A separate local web frontend connects to the original database implementation.

title: Systems Engineering Lab
description: A collection of five implementations that expose the mechanics behind everyday abstractions.
notes: Includes a Redis server, database engine, memory-backed agent, private search and C compiler.
Each implementation remains independently usable.
The lab’s own frontend exposes all five tools within that repository.

title: E-commerce Website Collection
description: An existing collection of storefront, checkout, registration and contact pages.
notes: Static website pages are preserved in the repository.
These pages are distinct from the React LaptopHub project described in the CV.
Original checkout/registration pages are demos, not production payment or account systems.

title: Birthday Website
description: An interactive, personal birthday website with a dedicated local preview.

title: Birthday · Photo Edition
description: A photo-based edition of the birthday website.

title: Meta-search Workspace
description: A starter search interface added to the previously empty meta-search repository.
notes: Uses the aggregator from the separate private-metasearch-engine repository.
Offline catalog with optional live Wikipedia lookup.

title: Copilot · School Activities
description: A learning repository with a school activities app and a persistent registration adapter.

title: OctoFit Tracker
description: A local fitness-tracking prototype alongside the Copilot course’s unfinished application skeleton.
notes: Working local workout log and leaderboard.
The added prototype is not completion of the course’s Django/MongoDB stack.

title: Stack Overflown
description: A developer-themed browser puzzle game in the Git introduction exercise repository.
